rule: This file is the ONLY source of anything that appears on screen or is spoken. Every string the film paints must trace to a claim id here.

claims.spoken: Alaska might hold thirty thousand kinds of insect
claims.label: per ADN, attributed to unnamed scientists
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska may contain as many as 30,000 insect species. Scientists have identified only about 9,000 of them."

claims.spoken: It has names for about nine thousand
claims.label: per ADN
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska may contain as many as 30,000 insect species. Scientists have identified only about 9,000 of them."
claims.note: ADN does not say whether 'identified' means described to science or recorded present in Alaska. The film must not resolve that ambiguity for them.

claims.spoken: Derek Sikes runs the insect collection at Alaska's Museum of the North
claims.on_screen: DEREK SIKES / CURATOR OF INSECTS / UA MUSEUM OF THE NORTH
claims.verbatim_source: "curator of insects for the University of Alaska Museum and a professor of entomology for the University of Alaska Fairbanks"
claims.note: corroborated by the UAF Museum's own entomology staff page

claims.spoken: Since two thousand six it's gone from a thousand records to four hundred thousand
claims.verbatim_source: "Since taking charge of the collection in 2006, Sikes has expanded it from roughly 1,000 records to more than 400,000, representing about 2 million specimens."
claims.note: second primary source, the museum's own collections page, gives about 425,000 records as of January 2026

claims.verbatim_source: "Since taking charge of the collection in 2006, Sikes has expanded it from roughly 1,000 records to more than 400,000, representing about 2 million specimens."
claims.note: HARD RULE: a RECORD is a catalog entry, a SPECIMEN is a physical insect. The film may never say '400,000 specimens' or '2 million records'.

claims.spoken: Every one that arrives is born digital
claims.label: Sikes, quoted by ADN
claims.verbatim_source: "It basically means that every specimen that comes in is born digital,"
claims.note: this refers to PHYSICAL BARCODE TRACKING LABELS at intake, NOT DNA barcoding. The film must never conflate the two senses.

claims.spoken: In two thousand eight, a paper taught a neural network to name a species from a stretch of one gene
claims.verbatim_source: field: title = "Inferring species membership using DNA sequences with back-propagation neural networks"; journal = "Systematic Biology"; year = 2008; volume_pages = "57(2), 202-215"; doi = "10.1080/10635150802032982"
claims.note: ABSTRACT ONLY was reached. Full text is paywalled. This is disclosed in the Gmail draft and the film states no methodological detail beyond the abstract sentence.

claims.spoken: Ninety seven point five percent, on eighty unknown ground beetles
claims.verbatim_source: "With a 630-to 690-bp fragment of the COI gene, we identified 97.50% of 80 unknown sequences of ground beetles, 95.63%, 96.10%, and 100% of 275, 205, and 9 unknown sequences of the neotropical skipper butterfly to their correct species, respectively."

claims.spoken: One of its four authors was Derek Sikes
claims.verbatim_source: field: authors = "A.B. Zhang, D.S. Sikes, C. Muster, S.Q. Li"
claims.note: same-person confirmation: the paper is listed on Derek S. Sikes's own Google Scholar profile, and the UAF Museum staff page identifies him as the curator

claims.spoken: Eighteen years later the list still grows about a thousand species a decade
claims.label: per ADN
claims.verbatim_source: "Every decade another 1,000 are added to the list."

claims.spoken: Twenty one thousand still unnamed. Two hundred ten years at that pace
claims.label: our arithmetic on ADN's two labeled figures, not an ADN projection
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: this is derived, 30,000 minus 9,000 is about 21,000, and 21,000 divided by 1,000 per decade is about 210 years

claims.spoken: Sweden started counting in the seventeen hundreds. Alaska's had less time and more ground
claims.label: per ADN, single-sourced
claims.verbatim_source: "Sweden first identified 1,000 insect species in the 1700s. More than 30,000 insect species have so far been identified in Sweden, which is at a similar latitude as Alaska but is smaller in area."

claims.spoken: A classifier needs a DNA sequence
claims.label: ADN describes sequencing as an identification clue
claims.verbatim_source: "DNA sequencing provides another clue. If an insect clearly belongs to a known group but its genetic information doesn't match anything in international databases, researchers may have found either an undocumented species or one that has never been sequenced before."

claims.label: the film's own statement of the evidentiary limit
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: the ADN profile contains zero mentions of AI, machine learning or neural networks, and no post-2008 statement from Sikes on automated identification was found

the_films_own_synthesis: The connection between the 2008 neural-network paper and the 2026 profile is THIS FILM'S synthesis. Neither ADN nor Sikes drew it. The film says so on screen and never implies otherwise.
never_say: that ADN reported an AI story (it contains zero mentions of AI, ML or neural networks)
that Sikes said the bottleneck is not algorithms
that the 2008 network was ever run on Alaska's collection
'400,000 specimens' or '2 million records' (the units are different and the difference is load-bearing)
that ADN's 'barcode' means DNA barcoding (it means physical tracking labels)
that the 210-year figure is an ADN projection (it is our arithmetic on their numbers)
that modern AI has been tried here and failed (there is no evidence either way)
